title: Fix it: include a field only when it applies
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

You are given a user record with optional fields like a phone number or a business title.

Return an object with the user's name always included, but only include the optional fields if they are not empty strings.

Never emit a field with a null value — if the field should not appear, omit it entirely.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ name: payload.name, phone: payload.phone if (payload.phone != ""), title: payload.title if (payload.title != "") }
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
forgets the parentheses, so the if modifies the value not the key
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ name: payload.name, (phone: payload.phone) if (payload.phone != ""), (title: payload.title) if (payload.title != "") }

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ name: payload.name, phone: payload.phone if (payload.phone != ""), title: payload.title if (payload.title != "") }

explanation.approach: Use `(key: value) if (condition)` to include a field conditionally. The parentheses wrap the key-value pair so the `if` applies to the whole pair. Without them, the `if` applies only to the value, creating a field with a null key.

snippets.label: A user record with optional fields
snippets.note: Some fields are empty strings — the job is to drop them from the output.

snippets.label: The answer — parentheses around the pair
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ name: payload.name, (phone: payload.phone) if (payload.phone != ""), (title: payload.title) if (payload.title != "") }
snippets.note: The `(phone: ...)` wraps both the key and value, so the `if` applies to the entire field. When `title` is empty, the whole field is omitted.

snippets.label: When all optionals are empty
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ name: payload.name, (phone: payload.phone) if (payload.phone != ""), (title: payload.title) if (payload.title != "") }
snippets.note: Both optional fields are empty, so they are dropped entirely. No null values appear.

snippets.label: Wrong approach — using a ternary instead
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ name: payload.name, phone: if (payload.phone != "") payload.phone else null, title: if (payload.title != "") payload.title else null }
snippets.note: This creates a null value when the condition fails. The field still appears in the output with a null value — exactly what the problem asked you NOT to do. The conditional field syntax `(key: value) if (...)` omits the entire field instead.

snippets.label: A record with all fields present
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ name: payload.name, (phone: payload.phone) if (payload.phone != ""), (title: payload.title) if (payload.title != "") }
snippets.note: All fields pass their conditions, so all appear in the output.
